text:
neha: Quick SOC2/ISO question from Fjord's security reviewer — do our hosted API logs ever persist plaintext customer emails or CC numbers? They want sample log snippets, retention window, list of subprocessors that might see logs, and confirmation of encryption in transit/at-rest. cc @sarah @tim

Tim: Short answer: we do automatic PII redaction for common patterns in request/response bodies. That said, if a customer includes an email as part of a request metadata field it can appear in traces before redaction heuristics run. We don't store credit-card numbers in plaintext (we strongly redact patterns). Example redaction snippet below:

```
user_email: <redacted_email>
card_number: <redacted>
ip: <redacted_ip>
trace_id: abc123
```

alina: For encryption at rest — hosted volumes and object storage use AES-256. S3 objects are SSE (AES256) by default and we support customer-managed CMKs in KMS for Dedicated. KMS key rotation policy: 90d for service-managed keys (customers can set longer for CMKs). For private/on-prem, depends on their infra and KMS.

security-bot: Policy links: https://redwood.internal/security/logging-redaction and https://redwood.internal/compliance/encryption. Quick checklist: logs_retention=90d default; access=role_based; exports require DTA + legal approval.

sarah: If they want log samples we can provide redacted exports, but we need signed NDA / data-sharing approval from Legal first. Please add the requested fields so Ops can produce a sample. I'll need ticket approval (RG-4321).

neha: They specifically asked for: 1) whether emails/IDs appear in logs, 2) retention window, 3) subprocessors list, 4) encryption in transit & at rest, 5) primary security contact. Drafting reply now. For subprocessors I have: AWS (S3, EC2), Fastly (edge), Datadog (metrics only), PagerDuty (alerts). Is that complete?

Tim: Add Cloudflare if customer's traffic hits our CDN. Important: Datadog receives metrics/aggregates only; we do NOT forward full request bodies to Datadog. Full logs live in S3 behind strict IAM.

alina: Confirming in-transit: TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3). Internal service-to-service uses mTLS. For Dedicated, customers can enable their own TLS termination.

sarah: I'll run the draft by Legal. Ops needs to approve any redacted sample export — once you post exact fields to redact I'll mark the ticket and approve.

neha: Thanks. One more: if Fjord requests a live review or session to view logs, what's the approval flow and who can grant temporary access?

Tim: Flow we use: request -> product-security triage -> Ops creates a timeboxed STS session or signed S3 URL (read-only) -> legal + account-owner approval required. Ops ensures CloudTrail auditing and scopes the token to a `fjord-` prefix.

alina: Agree. We use STS tokens with 1h expiry for timeboxed access and log the session. Any export to a third party needs a Data Transfer Addendum (DTA).

security-bot: Reminder: export to third party requires completed DTA. See https://redwood.internal/compliance/dta.

neha: Perfect. I'll assemble the response including the redaction snippet, subprocessors list (AWS, Fastly/Cloudflare, Datadog (metrics only), PagerDuty), encryption assertions, and the access flow + DTA note. Will attach to RG-4321 and post draft here for review before sending to Fjord.

sarah: Thanks — ping me when it's in RG-4321 and I'll fast-track the legal sign-off. :thumbsup:
